items.streamTitle: Earthquake shelter model counted usable housing, not just deliveries
items.streamSummary: A Wenchuan-based logistics simulation explicitly modeled road disruption and shelter setup delays. Coverage fell under disrupted routes, with no feasible plan under severe conditions; field outcomes were not tested.

items.streamTitle: War narratives revealed differences that symptom scores missed
items.streamSummary: A Lebanese observational study found non-linear differences in resilience and narrative expression across prewar, postwar and displaced groups. Selection and timing limit causal interpretation.

items.streamTitle: NATO is making reversible, conditions-based changes to KFOR
items.streamSummary: NATO described a new KFOR commander and gradual peacekeeping posture adjustments in Kosovo. Its stability assessment and planned adjustments are not proof of operational effect.

items.streamTitle: Causal-design review finds mostly favorable green-space health results
items.streamSummary: A review found 30 of 33 empirical studies using quasi-experimental methods reported at least one positive health association interpreted causally. Assumptions and bias still matter.
items.attribution: Ying et al. — Humanities and Social Sciences Communications (Systematic Review)

items.streamTitle: A 96-item questionnaire was cut to 34 with limited reported accuracy loss
items.streamSummary: Machine-learning selection reduced survey length using responses from 1,022 people. Reported prediction and measurement checks were encouraging, but independent population and construct validation remain necessary.

items.streamTitle: CERN and Mistral proposed a Large Physics Model
items.streamSummary: The institutions plan a model trained on simulated particle collisions for physics-analysis tasks. No finished system or verified performance was announced; the initiative remains a research proposal.

items.streamTitle: AI agents fused sensor readings and images to flag possible structural anomalies
items.streamSummary: A retrieval-enhanced multi-agent system generated region-specific assessments for a historic masonry structure. Its evidence traces are useful, but single-site testing does not establish reliable damage diagnosis.

items.streamTitle: New dataset links EEG during narrative viewing with platform engagement measures
items.streamSummary: A released dataset pairs EEG from 65 video viewers with participant measures and online engagement signals. It enables new research but does not itself validate prediction from brain signals to population behavior.

items.streamTitle: Risk seeking crossed motor and economic tasks, but error correction differed
items.streamSummary: Researchers found risk-seeking choices in both physical timing and numerical decisions, with important differences in adjustments after mistakes. Behavioral similarity is not proof of a single mechanism.

items.streamTitle: Automated grading missed many failures in simulated surgical-consent conversations
items.streamSummary: Clinicians found 38 rubric-level failures across 50 simulated consent sessions. Automated grading detected fewer than half under one aggregation method. This is a stress test, not a patient-outcome study.
items.attribution: Abou Mrad et al. — npj Digital Surgery

items.streamTitle: Drone-suspended radiation detector tested at contaminated cleanup site
items.streamSummary: A drone carried an experimental gamma detector above a remediation site to explore safer radiological mapping. Early field testing was reported, but comparative accuracy and safety effects have not been established.
items.attribution: U.S. Army Corps of Engineers and Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory — field report

items.streamTitle: Little evidence collectivism increases automatic imitation
items.streamSummary: Large cross-cultural experiments found imitation effects but little support for the predicted collectivism gradient. The result challenges a common claim while leaving room for context-specific differences.

items.streamTitle: NATO SHINE put new technologies into military-user experiments
items.streamSummary: NATO tested emerging concepts with operators in scenario-based activities at SHINE 2026. Its report explains the experimental process but provides no quantitative proof of battlefield effectiveness.
items.attribution: NATO Allied Command Transformation — official report

items.streamTitle: Army innovation contests target tactical power and cheaper interceptors
items.streamSummary: The Army detailed pitch competitions, prototype funding and a 2027 interceptor demonstration path. These are acquisition priorities and planned opportunities, not proof that solutions are field-ready.
items.attribution: U.S. Army Pathway for Innovation and Technology — announcement

items.streamTitle: Digital-use scores correlated with weaker school engagement, but the modeled direct effect was null
items.streamSummary: A survey of 437 high-school students found that higher scores on a digital-addiction scale coincided with feeling less important to others, lower life satisfaction, and lower school engagement. In a structural model, the direct digital-use-to-engagement path was not significant, although a small indirect association through anti-mattering and life satisfaction was. Because all measures were collected at one time, the analysis does not prove that digital use causes disengagement or that the intermediate variables transmit a causal effect. It is a useful example of why mediation diagrams require stronger evidence than correlations alone.

items.streamTitle: The same medical prompt improved one LLM sharply and reduced accuracy in others
items.streamSummary: Researchers evaluated 16 language models under seven prompting strategies using 475 questions from a Taiwanese medical-licensing examination. Baseline accuracy varied from 35.4% to 85.9%. Average prompt changes were modest, but individual model responses differed sharply: one configuration rose from 49.7% to 87.4%, while other models became less accurate. No prompt strategy consistently improved all systems. The benchmark tests examination knowledge, not clinical patient outcomes, and some subgroup comparisons involve few models. The practical lesson is to evaluate specific model–prompt pairs rather than assuming a favored prompting technique transfers reliably.
items.attribution: Tseng et al. — npj Digital Medicine

items.streamTitle: Retraction trends shifted around research-incentive reforms, but the timing does not prove causation
items.streamSummary: An interrupted time-series study of China-affiliated papers published from 1992 to 2020 examined misconduct-related retraction rates around major performance-evaluation reforms. The authors report changes in levels and trends near the 1995, 1998, and 2015 reforms, including a clearer post-1998 increase in STEM and a post-2015 acceleration in humanities and social sciences. The association raises serious questions about metric-based research incentives, but retractions are an imperfect proxy for misconduct. Changing detection, publication volumes, and other concurrent reforms mean the design does not demonstrate that the incentives themselves caused the observed shifts.
items.attribution: Meng, Huang & Wu — Humanities and Social Sciences Communications

items.streamTitle: An opinion-dynamics model predicted simulated consensus and polarization regimes, not real populations
items.streamSummary: Researchers combined attraction, repulsion, and noninteraction rules in an agent-based opinion model that can generate consensus, two camps, or several persistent clusters. An empirical threshold matched the direction of simulated phase changes in 86.7% of grid conditions; cluster-count estimates were within one of the simulated modal outcome in 82.26%. The model also showed sensitivity to randomness and starting conditions. The main limitation is decisive: both the predictor and its evaluation come from the same artificial system. No claim about forecasting real-world polarization is warranted without external validation.
items.attribution: Jing et al. — Humanities and Social Sciences Communications

items.streamTitle: AEGIS separated approval of new AI models from alarms about versions already in use
items.streamSummary: AEGIS is an executable governance framework for adaptive medical AI, combining new-data intake, retraining, monitoring, and four possible deployment decisions. It also raises a separate alarm when the already-released model may be deteriorating, including when no acceptable replacement exists. Demonstrations used sepsis prediction and brain-tumor segmentation, and a cross-site drift test reported improved discrimination. This is a proof of concept, not evidence of safer clinical outcomes. Its drift detection mainly captures changes in input distributions, leaving changes in the relationship between inputs and outcomes for future validation.
items.attribution: Afdideh et al. — npj Digital Medicine

items.streamTitle: Reward cues influenced choices less when people were told to forget them or had less working memory
items.streamSummary: Three experiments tested whether reward-associated cues guide behavior automatically or through conscious expectations. Participants first learned links among cues, actions, and monetary outcomes. A simulated software failure followed by instructions to disregard earlier cue learning substantially reduced cue-driven choices; a working-memory load also weakened the effect. Some response bias persisted despite both manipulations. This suggests that cue influence includes cognitive interpretation without ruling out automatic processes. The tasks involved artificial rewards, so their results should not be equated directly with persistent real-world habits or addictions.

items.streamTitle: Safe reinforcement learning has two different levers: change the goal or restrict dangerous exploration
items.streamSummary: A new review links animal learning and neuroscience to the engineering of safe reinforcement learning. It distinguishes changing the objective so harmful outcomes count more heavily from changing exploration so a learner avoids risky actions before it has reliable knowledge. Each approach entails assumptions and a possible tradeoff between safety and efficient learning. The paper synthesizes existing evidence rather than testing a new algorithm. Its practical value is a clearer design vocabulary: an agent can fail because it pursues the wrong objective, because it explores unsafely, or because a protective heuristic becomes overly restrictive.

items.streamTitle: Ukraine and NATO presented a drone-attack forecasting model ready for integration, without public accuracy metrics
items.streamSummary: Ukraine's defence ministry reported two AI tools developed with NATO: Model No. 13 forecasts the likely timing, location, intensity, and type of enemy drone activity using historical and current data, while Model No. 32 filters and ranks possible artillery plans. Officials say the forecasting model has been tested against real datasets and is ready for system integration; the planning prototype is still under testing. The release does not disclose forecast calibration, false alarms, operator use, or operational effects. It is evidence of development and transition readiness claims, not independently demonstrated battlefield advantage.
items.attribution: Ukraine Ministry of Defence / NATO-Ukraine JATEC

items.streamTitle: NATO Innovation Fund opened a Warsaw branch to connect startups with defense procurement
items.streamSummary: The NATO Innovation Fund, a €1 billion venture investor backed by 24 Allied countries, established a Warsaw branch and a new partnership with the Polish Dual-Use Chamber. Its regional team will identify deep-tech startups, help portfolio firms move from pilots toward procurement, and connect companies with governments and militaries on NATO's eastern flank. The announcement signals a concrete institutional investment in adoption, but it is not evidence that a new defense capability is effective or already deployed. Subsequent evaluation should examine actual contracts, field performance, integration, and sustainment.

items.streamTitle: A fuzzy Bayesian network organized public-health risk judgments, but did not validate outbreak forecasts
items.streamSummary: A new study builds a fuzzy Bayesian network to combine uncertain expert assessments of public-health emergency risk and illustrates the approach using COVID-19 in Wuhan. The resulting model classified that retrospective case as high risk and identified information sharing, coordination, and isolation measures as influential model factors. Those outputs depend on the network structure and supplied judgments; they are not prospectively verified risk estimates or measured effects of specific interventions. The practical contribution is a structured way to record uncertainty and interrogate scenarios, provided experts, assumptions, and predictive calibration remain visible.
items.attribution: Fu et al. — Humanities and Social Sciences Communications
